Triage: lands in `domain:devx` (`packages/core`'s contract pin + its timeout posture); rationale: class (a) — a reproducible defect with a **named cause**, which is what separates it from a shrug. The case awaits `import('./index.js')` inside the test body, so the whole `@objectstack/core` index graph is charged to a per-case 5000ms budget; vitest's own timing for the failing run was **5036ms**, and the per-file reporter attributes ~4-5s of run phase to that one await. ⇒ "Flake" is not the diagnosis here — the cost is measured and it sits a few tens of milliseconds under the ceiling. `Bug`.

⭐ The two-run comparison is doing real work: 1232 passed / 0 failed, then 1231 passed / 1 failed on the **same tree, same worktree**, differing only in load from sibling agents. Same input, different verdict ⇒ the pin's outcome is a function of the box, not of the code. That is the property that makes it worth fixing rather than re-running.

`priority:p3`, ⛔ not p2, and the line is a measurement nobody has taken: this has been observed **only on a shared dev box under sibling load**, ⛔ never on CI. Its sibling **#16434** (driver-sql's live PG + MySQL matrix, same default 5000ms) is the one that *"just dequeued an unrelated PR"* — an observed CI cost — and will grade higher when this seat reaches it. ⚠️ **Escalation criterion: the first time this case reds on `Test Core`, it is p2.** The contention shape is present there (four turbo tasks at `--concurrency=4` on a 4-vCPU runner), so this is a plausible trigger, not a remote one.

⛔ Do not treat the eventual red as an infra flake and re-run it. That is precisely the failure mode this card and #16434 exist to name: a pin that reds only under load reads as flaky, gets re-run, and trains everyone to discount reds from that file.

Route, and the card is right that the choice is not mechanical: hoisting the import to module top charges it to the **collect** phase, where no per-case timeout applies — but that changes *when* the module is loaded relative to the rest of the file, and this pin is asserting something about the published entry point ("reaches consumers through the package entry point, and is exactly two symbols", #13905). ⇒ Whoever takes it must first read what the pin claims about load **order**; if the assertion does not depend on the import happening inside the case, hoisting is the better fix because it removes the timing dependency instead of widening it. A deliberate per-case timeout is the fallback, ⛔ and if chosen it needs a comment saying what it is buying — an unexplained raised timeout is indistinguishable from one raised to silence a real regression.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.
